course_outline_concepts: Judge-LLM as eval primitive: MT-Bench, Arena-Hard, WildBench
Judge bias measurement: position swap, length-controlled pairs, confidence calibration
Con-J / Self-Taught Evaluators / J1 — 2024/25 synthetic-judge line applied to eval
Judge-RM vs generative-RM — when eval-time judge != RL-time RM matters
Why 'GPT-4-as-judge' is slowly being replaced and what by

sources.what_to_extract: MT-Bench 80 questions, 8 categories; GPT-4 vs human-expert agreement 85%+; position bias 22% flip rate for GPT-4, 40% for GPT-3.5; verbosity bias upward slope; self-enhancement matrix; mitigations (swap-and-average, length-controlled pairs, reference-guided, CoT judging).

GenRM scoring via verdict log-prob; CoT-RM critique-then-verdict 3-10 pp lift on RewardBench; rubric-steerability; GenRM vs scalar RM calibration curve; compute trade-off (slower, reuses base-LM stack).

Con-J noisy-negative trick; Self-Taught Evaluators iterative RewardBench — crosses GPT-4 at iter 3; J1 adds RL on judge CoT; ~40K synthetic pref pairs beat 2-40x more data; consistency-swap filter; judge-collapse / judge-as-weapon risks.
Soft labels from labeler logits; d-RLAIF reads reward from log-prob of 'Better' token; CoT preference prompt adds 3-5 pp; labeler-size monotone scaling; AI labels 100x cheaper per pair.

GPT-4 4-aspect rubric (instruction-following, truthfulness, honesty, helpfulness 0-10); judge-induced bias propagation into DPO models; model-fleet contamination (GPT-4 scores its own outputs); aspect conflation.
Joint-input cross-attention pairwise RM; swap-augmentation 2-3 pp; tournament O(N log N) aggregation; PairRM-0.4B matches scalar-RM-7B; DPO pair filtering use case.
Unhackability impossibility; Goodhart-on-judges = eval leakage when the same judge labels train prefs and ranks checkpoints; why bounded-evaluation protocols matter.
Policy-as-judge iter-3 plateau; judge-Spearman-with-humans rises 0.62->0.71; the judge-drift bound that motivates separating RL-time RM from eval-time judge.
Meta-judge role to evaluate judge; AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win-rate 22.9->39.4 over 4 iters; length-bias control in rubric; judge-DPO vs actor-DPO separation.
Average-metric-hides-tail principle transfers to judges: judge accuracy on aggregate hides per-slice calibration; external-verifier filter as an anchor against judge-induced drift.
Real-user logs as WildBench-style prompt source; realism anchor that synthetic MT-Bench misses; distribution gap between opt-in real chat and Evol-Instruct synthetic sets.

deliverables: figures/judge-bias.html (interactive bias explorer + calibration curve, self-contained, ~200-280 lines)
hard_rules: No external CDN references in HTML (inline CSS/JS only)
Quote attested numbers (GPT-4 22% position-flip, 85%+ human agreement, Self-Taught-Evaluator iter-3 GPT-4 crossover, Meta-Rewarding 22.9->39.4) directly; label inferred values when not attested
Three required tables: bias x measurement method x correction; MT-Bench / Arena-Hard / WildBench comparison; Con-J / STE / J1 contrast
Must quote Zheng 2023 judge-bias source directly (MT-Bench paper)
